title: Minor pentatonic
summary: Explore the five-note pattern with deliberate string changes.
goal: Learn the five-note pattern and controlled string changes.
body: First practice the major-scale lesson and individual string changes. A minor pentatonic contains root, minor third, fourth, fifth and minor seventh. Start at 50 BPM with quarters; ascend in bars 1–3 and descend in bars 4–6. The highest note is not necessarily the root. Keep one note sounding at a time; use short fragments before a full repeat at 60 BPM.
